Equal frequency binning

Source: R/rbin-equal-freq.R
rbin_equal_freq.Rd

Bin continuous data using the equal frequency binning method.

Usage

rbin_equal_freq(data = NULL, response = NULL, predictor = NULL, bins = 10)

# S3 method for class 'rbin_equal_freq'
plot(x, print_plot = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or tibble.

response

Bare column name, character name, or variable holding a character name in data. A binary variable coded as 0/1, a logical variable, or a two-level factor/character. For a two-level factor the first level is treated as 0 and the second as 1. A character response is sorted in byte (C-locale) order: uppercase before lowercase, ASCII before accented characters; use a factor to choose the event level. The second value is the event. Rows with a missing response are dropped with a warning.

predictor

Bare column name, character name, or variable holding a character name in data. A numeric predictor variable.

bins

Number of bins.

x

An object of class rbin_equal_freq.

print_plot

logical; if TRUE, prints the plot else returns a plot object.

...

further arguments passed to or from other methods.

Value

A list of class rbin_equal_freq with the following elements: bins, a data.frame with one row per group (plus a final row for missing values when present); method; vars; lower_cut; and upper_cut.

Details

Groups have approximately equal sizes and never split tied values. For each k = 1, ..., bins - 1, take the smallest observed value whose cumulative count reaches k * n / bins, where n is the number of non-missing predictors (the type-1 empirical quantile). All observations equal to that value stay in the lower group. The next distinct observed value is the scoring cut. Repeated cuts and cuts beyond the maximum are omitted; a message reports the requested and actual numbers of non-missing bins when fewer bins result. No bin is empty. Without ties, group sizes differ by at most one observation.

Both the top-level and table lower_cut/upper_cut fields contain the actual left-closed, right-open scoring intervals. The first and last intervals extend to negative and positive infinity; gaps go to the preceding group. rbin_create() reproduces the non-missing training counts using these intervals. Missing predictor values form a separate final group, and the equal frequency groups are built from non-missing values only. As with other numeric methods, missing predictors produce missing dummy indicators.

Examples

bins <- rbin_equal_freq(mbank, y, age, 10)
bins
